cases.prompt: A patient has normal resting arterial pressure but reduced renal perfusion and elevated sympathetic activity. Explain how a compensated value can coexist with impaired reserve, and propose one measurement that tests your explanation.

rubric.criterion: Identifies a feedback response that preserves pressure
Explains a cost or reduced reserve under challenge
Proposes a perturbation or independent readout such as orthostatic response, renal flow, or hormone level

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Renal-clearance ledger · milestone 1: Reference clearance. Use the project’s shared urine flow 1.0 mL/min, filtration-only reference (plasma 0.25, urine 30.0 mg/mL) and the A–C/glucose rows in the guide. Use the project reference marker (plasma 0.25 mg/mL, urine 30.0 mg/mL, flow 1.0 mL/min) to infer model GFR. Write the excretion rate before dividing by plasma concentration, and list the handling assumptions. Use the project guide in week 11 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Tracks mg/mL, mL/min and mg/min through the calculation.
Uses the reference rather than a transported solute as the model filtration standard.
States freely filtered, steady-state and no net reference transport assumptions.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Renal-clearance ledger · milestone 2: Filtered and excreted ledgers. Use the project’s shared urine flow 1.0 mL/min, filtration-only reference (plasma 0.25, urine 30.0 mg/mL) and the A–C/glucose rows in the guide. For project solutes A and B, calculate clearance, filtered load, excretion and fractional excretion using the reference GFR. Show the net rate needed to close each ledger and distinguish zero net transport from proof that no transport occurred. Use the project guide in week 11 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Uses the same reference GFR and stated flow for both solutes.
Reports each mass rate separately before classifying handling.
Labels fractional excretion as a fraction or percentage consistently.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Renal-clearance ledger · milestone 3: Net secretion and identifiability. Use the project’s shared urine flow 1.0 mL/min, filtration-only reference (plasma 0.25, urine 30.0 mg/mL) and the A–C/glucose rows in the guide. For project solute C, compare excreted and filtered mass rates and calculate the net tubular contribution. State which alternative gross secretion/reabsorption pairs would leave the same net result, and which model assumptions are essential. Use the project guide in week 11 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Infers the sign of net transport from a mass-rate difference.
Keeps net secretion distinct from gross transporter-specific flux.
Identifies freely filtered and no-metabolism assumptions before interpreting clearance.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Renal-clearance ledger · milestone 4: Transport maximum. Use the project’s shared urine flow 1.0 mL/min, filtration-only reference (plasma 0.25, urine 30.0 mg/mL) and the A–C/glucose rows in the guide. For the project glucose row (plasma 4.0 mg/mL, urine 105 mg/mL, flow 1.0 mL/min), compare filtered load minus the stipulated 375 mg/min Tm with observed excretion. Explain the sharp-threshold assumption and one reason not to export it to a real person. Use the project guide in week 11 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Computes filtered load on the same mass/time basis as Tm.
Checks predicted excretion against urine concentration times flow.
States that no splay or nephron heterogeneity is represented.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.

cases.prompt: Renal-clearance ledger · milestone 5: Report a bounded physiological inference. Use the project’s shared urine flow 1.0 mL/min, filtration-only reference (plasma 0.25, urine 30.0 mg/mL) and the A–C/glucose rows in the guide. Assemble the complete project ledger, with units, net-transport sign convention and a text description of any diagram. Add an independent conservation check and a short scope note distinguishing this invented steady-state model from a physiological measurement. Use the project guide in week 11 for the full supplied model. Save your calculation and reasoning privately; this self-check is ungraded.

rubric.criterion: Every row has a named denominator and consistent units.
The scope note distinguishes model assumptions, observations and inferred net handling.
No result is presented as a diagnosis, clinical measurement or handling protocol.

limitations: Checklist marks record the learner’s own self-review. Written reasoning is not automatically evaluated.
